codeReview.summary: Verified the feature commit b10ef622 plus the current on-disk tree. Satisfied: VAL-FND-001 (packages/zoned-time standalone with zero runtime deps, the 7 named helpers moved verbatim plus extras, packages/staffing/src/tz.ts is `export * from '@repo/zoned-time'`, staffing depends on it; I re-ran the reservations suite and the parent's gate confirms zoned-time 11 tests and staffing 634 tests pass); VAL-FND-002 (deps are only zod + @repo/zoned-time, grep confirms no Date.now(/fetch( in src, flags fold only literal true and force children false without the master, the exact 8 permissions and SENSITIVE_GRANTS, grantsSatisfying update-implies-read, impersonation stripping, 5 scopes, reservationsTokenClaimsSchema with typ 'rsv+jwt'/aud 'tenant-api-reservations-operator', TTL 900/300); most of VAL-FND-005 (all five precedence tiers, days_mask bit 0 = Monday, overnight end_min > 1440, effective_from/to filtering); most of VAL-FND-007 (best-fit scoring on wasted covers/priority/combo penalty/gap packing, bounded 1- and 2-step repair, detectConflicts kinds); VAL-FND-008 except the schema clause (13 statuses, G/O/S/V actors, consumesCapacity, quickActionsFor, 30-minute finished->seated undo, all 8 policy exports, MESSAGE_KINDS/scheduleFor/dedupeKey/channelsFor US-only SMS, normalizeGuestPhone shared with tenant-api auth, all 24 error codes); and the oracle/scale parts of VAL-FND-009 (300-run property suite passes, 120 tables/80 combos/900 bookings scale test passes under the implemented caps; `@repo/reservations/testing` is exported). Re-ran `cd packages/reservations && CI=true npx vitest run` (19 files / 60 tests pass). Verdict: fail. Eight blocking divergences from the approved contract: (1) an `arrived` reservation outside the freeze window is moved by planBooking/tryRepair and reflow, violating I5 as written in VAL-FND-007; (2) the engine expansion budgets are attached to the wrong operations (book capped at 200 instead of 2,000, reflow at 2,000 instead of 5,000); (3) validateConfig does not detect turn-time coverage of 1..party_max, the end_min - first_seating_min <= 1440 span, or invalid policy references, has no blocks schema, and returns a report object instead of ConfigIssue[]; (4) localToInstant has no `opts` and never returns null for gap minutes, so the contract's gap:'skip'/'after' and service-end overlap:'later' semantics are absent, and the contract's 90-minute fold and day_start_min +/-1 cases are untested; (5) staff channels hide pacing-breached slots instead of warning, and walk_in_only is not allowed for waitlist (the channel model also lacks native/voice_agent/host/waitlist); (6) no schema anywhere has the required ISO `expiresAt` + `now` deadline responses; (7) the property suite runs static scenarios only - no random operation sequences and no I1-I8 verification (I5/I6/I7/I8 are unchecked); (8) resolveServices ignores the contract's 'ordered by latest effective_from then priority' rule for weekly templates (no priority field at all). Four non-blocking issues: quiet hours default 22:00 and shift later vs the architecture/contract 21:00 and shift earlier (will fail VAL-MSG-016), MESSAGE_KINDS names diverge from architecture section 9.3, the status set/capacity model diverges from architecture section 6.4 (pending_approval/disputed vs requested/partially_arrived; pending_payment not capacity-consuming), and tenant-api auth now rejects numbers without a leading '+' that the previous helper accepted.

issues.description: I5 violation: `arrived` reservations are movable by repair and reflow. isBookingHardLocked (day-state.ts:118-133) treats only `seated`/`partially_seated` (line 125), `tableLocked` and the freeze window as immovable; `arrived` is in ACTIVE_BOOKING_STATUSES (engine/assign.ts:269-275) and therefore soft. Reproduced read-only with the package sources: assignTables (planBooking/tryRepair) with an `arrived` booking on t_med outside the 60-minute freeze and a 4-top request returns assigned:true with repairedMoves [{bookingId:'r_arrived', fromTableIds:['t_med'], toTableIds:['t_small']}]; reflowDay moves the same arrived booking when its table is blocked. VAL-FND-007 (validation-contract.md:45-49) requires that 'Neither tryRepair nor reflow ever moves a locked assignment, a reservation in partially_arrived/arrived/partially_seated/seated/finished, or a reservation within freeze_min of start_at (invariant I5)', and architecture.md:231-233 says '...or any reservation that has arrived, is seated, or is inside the freeze window'. The worker's I5 test (engine/assign.test.ts:249) only covers tableLocked/seated/freeze, so the contract's arrived case is untested. (The contract also names `partially_arrived`, a status that does not exist in state-machine.ts:4-18, so that half of the clause cannot be satisfied as written - but `arrived` does exist and is not protected.)

Expansion budgets are attached to the wrong operations, contradicting the contract and architecture. MAX_REPAIR_EXPANSIONS = 200 (assign.ts:23) hard-caps planBooking/assignTables: line 456-460 computes `Math.min(MAX_REPAIR_EXPANSIONS, input.maxExpansions ?? MAX_REPAIR_EXPANSIONS)`, so a caller cannot raise the book budget at all. MAX_DAY_EXPANSIONS = 2_000 (line 24) caps reflowDay (lines 917-921) and each per-booking repair inside reflow is additionally capped at 200 (line 1059). VAL-FND-009 (validation-contract.md:57-62) and architecture.md:1196-1197 ('Budgets: search 200 node expansions per slot, book 2,000, reflow 5,000 per call. Exhausting a budget returns "no fit" (never a partial plan)'), and the domain-worker skill step 3, all require search 200 per slot, book 2,000, reflow 5,000. Consequence: a booking that needs 201-2,000 repair expansions returns `assigned:false, reason:'repair_budget_exhausted'` (a false "no fit") where the approved budget requires success, and reflowDay stops at 2,000 instead of 5,000, marking the remaining soft bookings `unresolvable` - a partial outcome rather than the architecture's deterministic "no fit". Search per-slot repair is capped at 200 (engine/availability.ts:520-526), which matches the search budget, but the whole-day 2,000 cap (availability.ts:556-560) and the 5,000 calendar cap (availability.ts:46) are not the approved mapping. The scale test enshrines the wrong constants (engine/scale.test.ts:36,64). Note features.json expectedBehavior bullet 5 states MAX_REPAIR_EXPANSIONS = 200 / MAX_DAY_EXPANSIONS = 2000, which is what was implemented, but the contract is authoritative (per the review assignment) and the skill repeated the 200/2,000/5,000 mapping.

validateConfig does not implement several required VAL-FND-004 detections (validation-contract.md:27-31). (a) Turn-time buckets are only checked for gaps/overlaps *between* existing buckets within one serviceId group (validate.ts:419-465): nothing verifies the union covers `1..party_max` contiguously - no check that the first bucket starts at 1 or that the last reaches party_max - although architecture.md:600-603 says 'Validation: contiguous, non-overlapping ranges covering 1..party_max'. A config whose only bucket is minParty 3..4 for a location with maxParty 8 produces no issue. (b) The `end_min - first_seating_min <= 1440` rule is not checked; the service block (validate.ts:393-416) only verifies endMin > startMin and lastSeatingMin within [startMin, endMin]. (c) ValidateConfigInput (validate.ts:38-98) has no policies field and there is no policy-reference issue code, so 'invalid policy references' is never detected. (d) There is no strict Zod schema for blocks anywhere in src/config/ (config/index.ts exports settings/areas/tables/combinations/decor/floor-plan/services/turn-times/pacing/service-table-availability/special-days/policies only). (e) The function returns ValidateConfigReport (validate.ts:166-172) rather than the contract's `ConfigIssue[]`; callers must read `.issues`. The delivered test (config/config.test.ts:369-494) exercises only internal gaps/overlaps, so the missing detections are untested.

localToInstant does not have the contract's signature or gap/fold options. The implementation is `localToInstant(businessDate, localStartMin, timeZone)` returning `{instantMs, adjustedForGap, ambiguousFold}` and never null (time.ts:68-109), whereas VAL-FND-003 (validation-contract.md:21-25) and architecture section 6.1 (architecture.md:1160-1165) require `localToInstant(date, localMin, tz, opts)` with 'Slots use { gap: "skip", overlap: "earlier" }; service ends use { gap: "after", overlap: "later" }', and 'nonexistent gap minutes (02:00-02:59) return null with gap: "skip" ... and resolve after the transition with gap: "after"'. Reproduced: localToInstant('2027-03-14', 150, 'America/New_York') returns 2027-03-14T07:30:00Z with adjustedForGap:true instead of null; there is no way for a caller to request skip-vs-after. resolveServiceWindow (time.ts:174-195) resolves its end through localToInstant, so a service end inside the repeated hour picks the earlier occurrence instead of overlap:'later' (reproduced: window 01:15->02:45 on 2026-11-01 NY yields a 150-minute window; the contract's 90-minute booking 01:15->second 01:45 is only correct where callers compute end = start + duration, as searchAvailability does at availability.ts:471-473). The delivered test file (time.test.ts:9-96) uses different dates (2026-03-08/2026-03-29 vs the contract's 2027-03-14/2027-03-28) and contains no case for the contract's 90-minute fold or the day_start_min +/-1-minute boundary, so the contract's named boundary cases are unverified.

Staff channels hide pacing-breached slots instead of warning, and walk_in_only is not usable for waitlist. `if (!globalPacing.allowed) { continue }` (availability.ts:516-518) drops the slot for every channel; evaluatePacing (engine/pacing.ts:54-191) returns allowed:false for maxCoversPerSlot/maxPartiesPerSlot regardless of channel, and SearchAvailabilityResult (availability.ts:165-174) has no warnings field. Reproduced: with maxCoversPerSlot=2 and an existing 2-cover booking at 18:00, the 18:00 slot is absent for online, phone, walk_in and operator alike. VAL-FND-006 (validation-contract.md:39-43) requires 'Staff channels (phone, host, walk_in, waitlist) surface pacing breaches as warnings rather than hiding slots, and allow walk_in_only tables only for walk_in and waitlist'. The channel model itself (engine/day-state.ts:3-4: 'online'|'operator'|'phone'|'walk_in'|'voice') has no 'native'/'voice_agent' guest channels and no 'host'/'waitlist' staff channels, and isModeAllowedForChannel (day-state.ts:97-110) allows walk_in_only only for 'walk_in' - reproduced false for 'waitlist' - so a waitlist seating path cannot use walk_in_only tables through this API.

No deadline response schema carries ISO `expiresAt` and server `now`. A grep for expiresAt/now across packages/reservations/src/schemas returns no response fields (the only time field is internalTickRequestSchema.nowMs, schemas/internal.ts:123); the schemas are request DTOs plus internal context/tick payloads (schemas/index.ts exports common/setup/book/public/guests/waitlist/payments/experiences/reports/internal/voice). VAL-FND-008 (validation-contract.md:51-55) requires strict DTOs 'where every deadline response includes ISO `expiresAt` and server `now`', and architecture.md:1300-1301 repeats it for every public response carrying a deadline (hold, payment, large-party request, waitlist offer, notify-me). The required response schemas are absent, so the clause is unmet and untestable; the schemas test (schemas/schemas.test.ts) only covers request validation and the 24 error codes.

The property suite does not do what VAL-FND-009 requires. The only property test generates 300 static day scenarios (arbitraryDayScenario) and checks one assignment plus one search per scenario (engine.property.test.ts:12-123); there are no random operation sequences (search, hold, book, modify, cancel, seat, finish, no-show, block, settings edit, clock advance) and no per-step invariant verification. testing/oracle.ts verifyDayInvariants (oracle.ts:30-170) checks only double-booking on tables (I1/I2-style), holds, blocks, and party-size/active membership; it does not check I5 (locked/arrived never moves), I6 (atomic modify), I7 (search/book agreement) or I8 (monotonic release), and the test title claims 'I1-I7' while validation-contract.md:57-62 requires 'invariants I1 through I8 after every step with zero soundness failures'. The skill's property list (SKILL.md step 3: no double booking; live hold consumes and expired does not; locked assignments never move; any returned slot can be held; cancelling/finishing never removes availability; overbook isolation; failed modify changes nothing) is likewise not covered. The scale test covers only the budget assertions.

Weekly-template ordering by latest effective_from then priority is not implemented. sortServices (resolve-services.ts:262-268) sorts by sortOrder -> startMin -> id; WeeklyServiceTemplateInput (resolve-services.ts:4-30) has no `priority` field, and effective_from/effective_to are only date-range filters in matchesWeekdayAndEffectiveRange (lines 276-283). VAL-FND-005 (validation-contract.md:33-37) requires weekly templates 'ordered by latest `effective_from` date, then `priority`', and architecture.md:618 repeats '(latest effective_from, then priority)'. Two overlapping versions of a template (e.g. a seasonal override with a later effective_from) are both returned in sortOrder order, so the newest template is never deterministically preferred; the delivered test only asserts sortOrder ordering (rules/resolve-services.test.ts:71-83) and never exercises priority.

Quiet-hours default and shift direction diverge from the approved design. scheduleFor defaults to 22:00-08:00 (messages.ts:78-79) and shifts non-urgent messages to the next 08:00 (later, lines 149-158), while architecture.md:1634 specifies 'default 21:00-08:00 location time' and VAL-MSG-016 (validation-contract.md) requires a send_at 'moved earlier out of quiet hours'. The delivered test hardcodes 22:00 (messages.test.ts:24), so the default is not pinned to the approved value. VAL-FND-008 only says 'quiet-hours shifting/skipping', so this is not a foundation blocking item, but the guest-messages milestone (VAL-MSG-016) will fail unless messages.ts is corrected.

MESSAGE_KINDS names diverge from architecture section 9.3 (architecture.md:1614-1615): 'modified' vs 'modification', 'cancelled' vs 'cancellation_guest'/'cancellation_restaurant', 'reminder_24h'/'reminder_2h' vs 'reminder', 'waitlist_table_ready' vs 'waitlist_ready', 'notify_slot_opened' vs 'notify_available'. The foundation contract does not enumerate kinds, but the guest-messages and waitlist milestones assert these names in meta.messageKind and email captures (VAL-MSG-011/012/013), so the canonical list will need reconciliation before those milestones.

The status set and capacity model diverge from architecture section 6.4 (architecture.md:1226-1232): the implementation has pending_approval and disputed (plus no partially_arrived) instead of requested and partially_arrived, and consumesCapacity (state-machine.ts:32-40) excludes pending_payment although architecture says capacity is consumed in pending_payment until payment_expires_at. VAL-FND-008 only says 'all 13 statuses' (13 exist) and the contract itself uses pending_approval at line 537, but VAL-ONLINE references status `requested` (validation-contract.md:1675), so the names need reconciling before later milestones; no validator-visible foundation failure today.

Phone normalization in customer auth was tightened beyond the previous behavior. auth.ts now normalizes with normalizeGuestPhone and validates with /^\+[1-9]\d{6,14}$/ (packages/reservations/src/phone.ts:3-8), which requires a leading '+'; the removed helpers accepted an optional '+' (/^\+?[1-9]\d{6,14}$/) and did not convert '00'. A customer entering a country-code number without '+' (e.g. '14155552671', '966501234567') now gets 400 'Invalid phone number' on OTP request/verify where it previously passed; '00...' forms are newly accepted. The new auth.test.ts only covers '+1 (415) 555-2671' and '00966...'. This is a behavior change in a shared auth path that the handoff's discoveredIssues did not flag; decide whether the stricter E.164-only rule is intended.

sharedStateObservations.observation: features.json for this feature contradicts the authoritative budget mapping, and the worker followed features.json. expectedBehavior bullet 5 says 'bounded repair (MAX_REPAIR_EXPANSIONS = 200), soft-booking reflow (MAX_DAY_EXPANSIONS = 2000)', while validation-contract.md:57-62, architecture.md:1196-1197 and the domain-worker skill step 3 all require search 200 per slot, book 2,000, reflow 5,000. The worker implemented the features.json numbers and reported skillFeedback.followedProcedure=true with no deviations, so the contradiction between features.json and the contract/architecture/skill is a shared-state defect that misled this worker (and is the root of blocking finding 2). Recommend reconciling the features.json wording (or noting the contract governs) so later workers do not repeat it.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: features.json expectedBehavior bullet 5; validation-contract.md:57-62; architecture.md:1196-1197; skills/domain-worker/SKILL.md step 3 ('Budget tests: the engine stops at the approved expansion budgets (search 200 per slot, book 2,000, reflow 5,000)'); packages/reservations/src/engine/assign.ts:23-24,456-460,917-921; handoff.skillFeedback

sharedStateObservations.observation: The domain-worker skill step 3 lists specific engine property tests (no double booking; a live hold consumes capacity and an expired one does not; locked assignments never move; any slot a search returns can be held immediately; cancelling or finishing never removes availability; online booking never uses capacity created by a staff overbook; a failed modification changes nothing), but the delivered property suite covers none of those scenarios - only a static scenario + oracle assignment check and slot tableIds (engine.property.test.ts), and verifyDayInvariants checks only double-booking/holds/blocks/membership. The handoff nevertheless reports followedProcedure=true with no deviations. Either the skill's list is not being enforced during scrutiny or the feedback is inaccurate; the skill should also state the contract's operation-sequence requirement explicitly so workers know a scenario-only suite does not satisfy VAL-FND-009.

The skill step 5 requires keeping the public API exactly as architecture.md names it and explaining any deviation (missing parameter, name collision) in the handoff. This feature deviates in several APIs without a recorded deviation: localToInstant lost the `opts` parameter (architecture.md:1160-1165), resolveServices takes (businessDate, services, specialDays) or ({services}, businessDate) and returns ResolvedDayServices instead of the contract's ResolvedService[] (validation-contract.md:33-37), validateConfig returns a report object instead of ConfigIssue[], and the channel/status vocabularies differ from the architecture. The handoff's skillFeedback.deviations is empty, so reviewers cannot see which deviations were deliberate.

The architecture's quiet-hours rule (default 21:00-08:00, move scheduled reminders earlier) was missed and is not called out anywhere the worker could see it in the feature brief: the feature description only says 'message schedule and dedupe helpers', and the worker's test hardcodes 22:00 with a later shift. Adding the quiet-hours default/direction to the feature description or library would prevent the guest-messages milestone from inheriting the wrong behavior.

The shared-phone refactor changed tenant-api auth behavior (numbers without a leading '+' are now rejected, '00' prefixes are now accepted) without being listed in handoff.discoveredIssues or documented. library/staffing-patterns.md / the mission docs do not mention that @repo/reservations now owns phone normalization for customer auth; a note in the library would help later auth workers and validators who test phone login formats.

summary: Reviewed fnd-zoned-time-and-reservations-domain (commit b10ef622, worker 56987751, domain-worker skill). The extraction (VAL-FND-001) and the pure-domain boundaries/flags/permissions/token claims (VAL-FND-002) are solid, and most of VAL-FND-005/006/007/008 is implemented and tested; I re-ran @repo/reservations (19 files/60 tests pass). Verdict: fail, with eight blocking contract divergences, each reproduced by reading or executing the package sources read-only: (1) arrived reservations are moved by tryRepair/reflow (I5, VAL-FND-007); (2) planBooking is capped at 200 expansions and reflow at 2,000, not the approved 2,000/5,000 (VAL-FND-009, architecture.md:1196-1197); (3) validateConfig misses turn-time coverage of 1..party_max, the end_min-first_seating_min<=1440 span and invalid policy references, has no blocks schema, and returns a report instead of ConfigIssue[] (VAL-FND-004); (4) localToInstant lacks the opts parameter and the null/gap:'skip' semantics, and service ends do not use overlap:'later'; the contract's 90-minute fold and day_start_min +/-1 cases are untested (VAL-FND-003); (5) staff channels hide pacing-breached slots instead of warning and walk_in_only is not allowed for waitlist (VAL-FND-006); (6) no schema has the required ISO expiresAt + now deadline responses (VAL-FND-008); (7) the property suite runs static scenarios only, with no operation sequences and no I1-I8 verification (VAL-FND-009); (8) weekly templates are not ordered by latest effective_from then priority (VAL-FND-005). Non-blocking: quiet hours default/direction (22:00, shifts later) vs architecture/VAL-MSG-016 (21:00, shifts earlier); MESSAGE_KINDS naming; state-machine status/capacity divergence from architecture section 6.4; and the tenant-api auth phone-normalization tightening. Shared-state observations flag the features.json budget wording that contradicts the contract/skill, the skill's property-test list not being followed despite followedProcedure=true, unreported API deviations, the missing quiet-hours note, and the undocumented phone-auth behavior change.
